velocity.label: Release velocity
velocity.definition: How fast the ball travels as it leaves the hand, in miles per hour.
velocity.direction: At the same release distance, a faster pitch gives the hitter less time. A slower changeup can widen the timing gap from your fastball.
velocity.context: Compare the same pitch type, device and throwing intent across sessions.

ivb.label: Induced vertical break
ivb.definition: How far above or below a gravity-only trajectory the pitch arrives, in inches.
ivb.direction: A more positive value means less drop. A negative value means extra drop. A four-seamer and a curve can benefit from opposite shapes.
ivb.context: A fastball with positive IVB can still travel downward. Compare pitches at similar speeds and release points.

hb.label: Horizontal break
hb.definition: How far the pitch bends sideways during flight, in inches.
hb.direction: The sign gives direction. On the Arsenal chart, +12 is twelve inches to the pitcher’s right and −12 is the same amount to the left.
hb.context: Arm side is right for a right-hander and left for a left-hander. Check the viewing convention on your source before comparing pitches.

spin.label: Spin rate
spin.definition: How many revolutions the ball makes per minute at release.
spin.direction: Higher RPM means faster rotation. Lower RPM means slower rotation. Either can suit a pitch, depending on its purpose and spin direction.
spin.context: Compare spin with velocity, axis and measured movement. Two pitches with the same RPM can break differently.

axis.label: Spin axis
axis.definition: The orientation of the line the ball rotates around. A device may express the direction as an angle or a clock-face tilt.
axis.direction: Angles wrap around. For example, 359° and 1° are only two degrees apart. Clock positions describe directions without ranking them.
axis.context: Compare the same viewpoint and axis convention. A camera-relative tilt needs a known view to interpret it as pitcher-relative.

efficiency.label: Spin efficiency
efficiency.definition: The percentage of total spin rotating across the flight path and contributing to spin-induced deflection.
efficiency.direction: A higher percentage means more transverse spin. A lower percentage means more spin around the flight direction, as on a gyro slider.
efficiency.context: Judge the percentage alongside the intended pitch shape, total spin and measured break.

extension.label: Release extension
extension.definition: How far toward home plate the ball is released from the pitching rubber, in feet.
extension.direction: More extension shortens the remaining flight distance. Less extension leaves a longer flight at the same mound distance.
extension.context: Compare pitches at the same speed and mound distance. A repeatable release helps explain changes between sessions.

releaseHeight.label: Release height
releaseHeight.definition: The height of the ball above the ground at release, in feet.
releaseHeight.direction: A higher reading means a taller release point. A lower reading means the ball left the hand closer to the ground.
releaseHeight.context: Compare with your own release point for this pitch. Stature, arm slot and delivery affect the reading.

releaseSide.label: Release side
releaseSide.definition: The sideways offset of the release point from the rubber’s centerline, in feet.
releaseSide.direction: On the Arsenal chart, positive is to the pitcher’s right and negative is to the left. A value near zero is closer to the centerline.
releaseSide.context: Check your device’s viewpoint. Your position on the rubber and arm slot both affect this reading.

count.label: Pitch count
count.definition: The number of throws represented by a reading or an average.
count.direction: A larger count gives more throws to compare. An average based on one or two pitches can change sharply with the next throw.
count.context: If a count is missing from a pitch average, leave it blank. A row of data can represent a single throw or a whole session.

location.label: Pitch location
location.definition: Where the ball crosses the front of home plate, viewed against the strike zone.
location.direction: Higher and lower describe the height of the crossing. The best location depends on the target, count, pitch and hitter.
location.context: Compare the crossing with the intended target. A pitch outside the zone can be an intentional chase pitch.

stuff.label: Stuff+
stuff.definition: A model score comparing pitch characteristics with a professional pitch-family reference. The reference average is 100.
stuff.direction: Above 100 rates higher in the model. Below 100 rates lower. A score of 105 does not mean five percent more movement or five percent more outs.
stuff.context: Pitch Nav uses speed and available movement for its projections. Command and the outcome of a specific pitch are separate. The website preview shows a fictional score.

pitchType.label: Pitch type
pitchType.definition: The pitch family or grip the throw is labeled with, such as a four-seam fastball, slider or changeup.
pitchType.direction: These are categories. There is no higher or lower type.
pitchType.context: Use consistent tags when comparing your sessions. The same pitch name can cover different speeds and movement shapes.

armSlot.label: Arm slot
armSlot.definition: The angle of the throwing arm relative to the ground at release.
armSlot.direction: A higher slot is closer to overhand. A lower slot is closer to sidearm.
armSlot.context: 42° is an example for this report layout, not a measurement of the pitcher shown.

hipShoulder.label: Hip–shoulder separation
hipShoulder.definition: The difference between the direction the pelvis faces and the direction the shoulders face at the same instant.
hipShoulder.direction: A larger angle means the two are turned farther apart at that moment. The timing matters as much as the size of the angle.
hipShoulder.context: 38° is an example. One side view alone does not establish a precise 3D rotation.

stride.label: Stride length
stride.definition: How far the pitcher strides toward the target by lead-foot contact, expressed here as a percentage of standing height.
stride.direction: A larger percentage means a longer stride relative to that pitcher’s height. Longer is not automatically better.
stride.context: 87% is an example. Measuring this percentage requires a consistent starting point, scale and standing height.
